newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo securities agency approves new share issues.
newsitem.headline: Yugo securities agency approves new share issues.

text.p: The Yugoslav Securities Commission (YSC) has approved new share issues by five banks totalling 46.3 million dinars ($9.3 million), the YSC said in a statement on Monday.
Kulska banka received approval for a 35 million dinar share issue, the statement said.

The YSC granted approval for a five million dinar issue to Niska banka. Depozitno-kreditna banka and Novosadska banka will issue shares worth three million dinars each, while Yuco banka was granted approval for 300,000 dinars issue.

According to the YSC statistics for January-July period, the YSC granted approval to 21 banks and companies for a total of 166.454 individual shares. The value of all approved share issues stood at 141.85 million dinars.
No bank or company with an approved share issue has entered the bourse yet.

The YSC has repeatedly insisted on shares being sold on the bourse in order to create a real capital market in Yugoslavia. So far, all efforts have been fruitless because some key financial market institutions are still absent.
"We need investment banks, investment funds, rating agencies and strong managerial teams...in order to create a capital market," said Stojan Dabic, head of the Financial Market Development Centre.

Economists agreed any YSC campaign aimed at developing a capital market in Yugoslavia is unrealistic until the economy undergoes a genuine mass privatisation, free market reforms and achieves overall stability.
But the YSC seems determined to push banks and companies with approved share issues to come to the market.
"Together with banks and their management, the YSC will take steps to make sure that parts of those issues are sold on the bourse," the YSC said in its press release.
"It has to start some time, and we have firm promises from one bank to sell one third of its newly approved issue on the bourse," a senior YSC official who insisted not to be named told Reuters.
The official said the YSC hoped the first sale (of shares) on the bourse to happen during December.

"We have also given a go-ahead for new rules for shares (market) quotation and expect shares to appear on the bourse by the end of this year," the official said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
